[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]Los Vales stretches along the Pacific coast of the old American West, from the industrial north of Buffalo to the mountains of Fortuna, with the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Escaldar[/color][/url][color=white] desert at its back. A single highway, Route 69, ties all seven cities together. Off the road there is almost nothing left: the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832736][color=#7FDBFF]Urban Monopolization[/color][/url][color=white] emptied every small town, and the rest of the map belongs to deserts, mines, labor camps and corporate land.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]See the colored map of the seven states and their capitals in the Bubblepedia article [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2833664][color=#7FDBFF][b]Los Vales[/b][/color][/url][color=white].[/color]

[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]ROUTE 69[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The spine of the country: a single highway from the port of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Ferox[/color][/url][color=white] to the southern border, through all seven cities. It was bombed into a chain of craters in the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832554][color=#7FDBFF]Reunification War[/color][/url][color=white] of 2049 and rebuilt end to end by the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2834884][color=#7FDBFF]Rebirth Plan[/color][/url][color=white]. Today it is run by [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Trans Vales[/color][/url][color=white], with tolls every 50 kilometers, and shared by [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Coyote Cabs[/color][/url][color=white], [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]AquaVale[/color][/url][color=white] water convoys, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Pizza 69[/color][/url][color=white] drones, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Thirsty[/color][/url][color=white] — and, once a year, the illegal [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69 Race[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]

[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]THE ESCALDAR DESERT[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The great desert at the back of the country, once [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832744][color=#7FDBFF]Xinko-Xenko[/color][/url][color=white] land. Today it holds the AquaVale aquifers, the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Verdana[/color][/url][color=white] greenhouses, the old [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]BeDay[/color][/url][color=white] oil fields, the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Lockwell[/color][/url][color=white] labor camps and the quarry of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832678][color=#7FDBFF]Cauldron of Death[/color][/url][color=white]. Deep inside, at [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832744][color=#7FDBFF]Koxez-Kaya Nova[/color][/url][color=white], the Xinko-Xenko guard the last natural fields of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832745][color=#7FDBFF]Xunaya[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]

[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]THE COAST[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Los Vales faces the Pacific, and the sea is as owned as the land. The [/color][color=white][b]Pacific trade lane[/b][/color][color=white] leaves the Port of Ferox for the ports of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832728][color=#7FDBFF]Pacific Union[/color][/url][color=white]. Offshore stand BeDay's sea launch platform for its heaviest rockets and the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF][b]Zyx[/b][/color][/url][color=white][b] Floating Lab[/b][/color][color=white], officially a "wellness retreat", where nobody is allowed to dock. Off Tampa lies [/color][color=white][b]Lockwell Island[/b][/color][color=white], the maximum-security prison for debtors who tried to run. Further south, the rusting [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832712][color=#7FDBFF][b]Dinoco[/b][/color][/url][color=white][b] Platform[/b][/color][color=white] still stands where it exploded in 2006, and beyond [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Valewood[/color][/url][color=white] stretches the [/color][color=white][b]Dead Zone[/b][/color][color=white], a toxic tide where no fish has lived since 2055. Along the southern coves, smugglers land whatever the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999871][color=#7FDBFF]black market[/color][/url][color=white] needs.[/color]

[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]INFRASTRUCTURE[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The [/color][color=white][b]Port of Ferox[/b][/color][color=white], the largest in the country, and the [/color][color=white][b]Ferox Spaceport[/b][/color][color=white], from where BeDay Astral launches its mining ships and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2835114][color=#7FDBFF]Apogee Orbital[/color][/url][color=white] flies the rich to [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Paradise Station[/color][/url][color=white]. The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF][b]LV Airways[/b][/color][/url][color=white][b] hub[/b][/color][color=white] near [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]La Maria[/color][/url][color=white] — the airport whose construction cost the Xinko-Xenko their capital in 2007. AquaVale's desalination plants on the coast, Bastion's data centers in the Nakama State, and, sealed since 2022, the [/color][color=white][b]old [/b][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF][b]WM[/b][/color][/url][color=white][b] nuclear bases[/b][/color][color=white] of Coronnel, where the bomb that won the independence was found.[/color]

Crime, bad implants, poisoned air and people who think the world is a dream are part of daily life — the country is [/color][color=white][b]dangerous[/b][/color][color=white]. This page lists the main risks and how to survive them, for anyone who lives here or plans to visit.[/color]

[color=#FCFE76][i]"Welcome to Los Vales. Your safety is your responsibility." — sign at every border crossing[/i][/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/dg-dreamwalker.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]Officially they are [/color][color=white][b]the Ruptured[/b][/color][color=white]; in [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832688][color=#7FDBFF]Anchor Squad[/color][/url][color=white] reports they are [/color][color=white][b]RDS[/b][/color][color=white] — Reality-Detached Subjects ("an RDS was neutralized in [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Ferox[/color][/url][color=white]"). On the street everyone calls them [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832732][color=#7FDBFF][b]dreamwalkers[/b][/color][/url][color=white].[/color]

[color=white]Dreamwalkers are victims of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832732][color=#7FDBFF]Rupture[/color][/url][color=white]: people who spent so long in [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832550][color=#7FDBFF]Psychoverses[/color][/url][color=white] that they started seeing the real world as one more dream — a place where nothing matters, nobody is real and nothing can be punished. The worst cases mix too much Psychoverse with [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Zyx[/color][/url][color=white] combat stimulants and cheap implants. A dreamwalker with metal arms, convinced the world is a dream, is the most dangerous thing that can walk a street in Los Vales.[/color]

[color=white]Since the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832550][color=#7FDBFF]Total Connection[/color][/url][color=white], not a week passes without a dreamwalker being shot down in one of the seven cities. Only the Anchor Squad is authorized to face them. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]LVN[/color][/url][color=white] calls the attacks "isolated outbreaks".[/color]

[color=white][b]If you meet one:[/b][/color][color=white] do not argue, do not run in a straight line, never try to "wake them up". Get out of their line of sight and call the Anchor Squad — the bill comes later.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/dg-gangs.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]Petty crime.[/b][/color][color=white] Theft, robbery and vandalism are part of daily life, above all in busy centers and public transport. Never display valuables — and in Los Vales, your arm may be a valuable.[/color]

[color=white][b]Implant theft.[/b][/color][color=white] The Scrappers of Ferox tear implants out of living people in back alleys and sell them on the black market. A [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Kizuna[/color][/url][color=white] arm is the most stolen object in the country.[/color]

[color=white][b]Gang territories.[/b][/color][color=white] Whole districts are run by criminal organizations that work as parallel governments, with extortion, territorial wars and no security at all: [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Ashes[/color][/url][color=white] and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Scrappers[/color][/url][color=white] in Ferox, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Beacons[/color][/url][color=white] in the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Illuminated Favela[/color][/url][color=white], [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Thirsty[/color][/url][color=white] on [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69[/color][/url][color=white], [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Extras[/color][/url][color=white] in [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Valewood[/color][/url][color=white], the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]Brotherhood of Smoke[/color][/url][color=white] in [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]La Maria[/color][/url][color=white], the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]Death Cards[/color][/url][color=white] beneath [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Las Noites[/color][/url][color=white] — and the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832717][color=#7FDBFF]Golden Mafia[/color][/url][color=white], which owns [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Las Dulces[/color][/url][color=white]. In the outskirts, smaller gangs fight over every block.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/ad-dg-1.gif[/img][/align]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/dg-black-market.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]The black market sells everything: high-tech products of low quality, weapons, drugs and second-hand implants. Badly made goods explode, short-circuit and poison — a pirate implant can take your arm with it. And dealing with the market often means violence and extortion. Unlabeled doses of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832550][color=#7FDBFF]Psychoactive Reality[/color][/url][color=white] are the fastest road to the Rupture.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/dg-net.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832553][color=#7FDBFF]W-Net[/color][/url][color=white] is safe from hackers — and fully watched: everything you do there has your name on it, and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Panoptica[/color][/url][color=white], [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Asclepius[/color][/url][color=white] and the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999866][color=#7FDBFF]Cabinet[/color][/url][color=white] can read it. The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832553][color=#7FDBFF]C-Nets[/color][/url][color=white] belong to the corporations, and so does everything you put in them.[/color]

[color=white]The real danger is the [/color][color=white][b]Net[/b][/color][color=white], the old internet sealed since the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832553][color=#7FDBFF]Great Corruption[/color][/url][color=white]. It is full of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832715][color=#7FDBFF]Fragments[/color][/url][color=white], viruses, black markets and files from before 2044 — and it is the only place nobody watches. Hackers who go too deep come back with burned implants, broken minds, or not at all. Some come back repeating phrases about chains and switches. Crossing [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832553][color=#7FDBFF]the Seal[/color][/url][color=white] is a crime, and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Cerberus[/color][/url][color=white] does not arrest: it raids.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/dg-pollution.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]Intense industry and no environmental regulation left Los Vales with some of the worst air and water in the world. The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832687][color=#7FDBFF]ALCHACAL[/color][/url][color=white] gas turned the sky hazy cyan; acid rain eats paint, cars and skin; respiratory disease is the leading cause of death in Ferox. Global warming made disasters more frequent — earthquakes and, above all, floods, which collapse overpasses and drag whole slopes down. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832687][color=#7FDBFF]Fresh Air Co[/color][/url][color=white] sells breathable air by the hour; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]AquaVale[/color][/url][color=white] sells drinkable water by the liter.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]LIMITED ACCESS TO BASIC SERVICES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Almost every essential service is private — police, firefighters, health, water, schools. Rich districts get elite schools, the best hospitals and trained guards; the outskirts get whatever is cheap. Back-street clinics sell treatments nobody checks, and the firefighters only save insured buildings. See the Cabinet page for who runs what — and why even the State charges for it.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/dg-risk.png[/img][/align]

[align=center][background=#FF0276][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/h-dg-map.png[/img][/background][/align]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/dg-map.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]The hotter the color, the worse the odds: red where crime, dreamwalkers and pollution are all extreme — Ferox, the ruins of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832719][color=#7FDBFF]Hermosa[/color][/url][color=white], the Illuminated Favela and the Dead Zone offshore; green only inside the walls of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Zyxtopia[/color][/url][color=white], under the Dome of Las Noites and in the valleys of La Maria. Route 69 is never safe after dark.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][background=#FF0276][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/dangers/h-survival.png[/img][/background][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]EVERY DAY[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]1. Constant monitoring.[/b][/color][color=white] Use personal tracking and safety apps to get alerts about dangerous areas — and remember that Panoptica reads them too. [/color][color=white][b]2. Cyber protection.[/b][/color][color=white] Stay on the W-Net; never cross the Seal. [/color][color=white][b]3. Personal security.[/b][/color][color=white] Most Valians carry a weapon or a defense implant, especially in high-crime areas. [/color][color=white][b]4. Avoid risk areas.[/b][/color][color=white] Learn which districts to avoid and plan safe routes.[/color]

[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]GETTING AROUND[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]5. Safe transport.[/b][/color][color=white] Use armored vehicles or trusted transport; never ride an unsupervised bus — and check your balance before entering a Coyote Cab. [/color][color=white][b]6. Self-defense.[/b][/color][color=white] Training in self-defense or firearms is common, and legal. [/color][color=white][b]7. Identification.[/b][/color][color=white] Always carry your Citizen ID to cross areas watched by corporations and private security. [/color][color=white][b]8. Local news.[/b][/color][color=white] Follow security news and corporate events — but remember who owns LVN.[/color]

[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]IN THE CITIES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]9. Encrypted devices.[/b][/color][color=white] Prefer secure communication — if anything on the W-Net can be called secure. [/color][color=white][b]10. Dreamwalkers.[/b][/color][color=white] Watch for strange behavior, especially from people who speak as if nothing were real, and avoid direct confrontation. [/color][color=white][b]11. Corporate rules.[/b][/color][color=white] Learn the rules of the megacorps that own your district; breaking them can be worse than breaking the law.[/color]

[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]HEALTH[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]12. Pollution.[/b][/color][color=white] Wear masks and air filters in polluted areas, and keep a first-aid kit. [/color][color=white][b]13. Substances.[/b][/color][color=white] Be careful with Psychoactive Reality and any unlabeled dose, common at parties and clubs. [/color][color=white][b]14. Health plan.[/b][/color][color=white] Have a private plan with emergency cover — and know your [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832742][color=#7FDBFF]Life Score[/color][/url][color=white] before you need it.[/color]

[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]EMERGENCIES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]15. Support network.[/b][/color][color=white] Build a network of trusted contacts. [/color][color=white][b]16. Community.[/b][/color][color=white] Join local groups to share safety tips. [/color][color=white][b]17. Escape plans.[/b][/color][color=white] Always have a way out in case of attacks or corporate conflicts. [/color][color=white][b]18. Disaster kit.[/b][/color][color=white] Keep water, food, tools and documents ready — and an insurance policy that covers floods.[/color]

[color=white]Follow these rules and you will probably survive Los Vales. Probably.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#FD0377][b]FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]What do I do if I see a dreamwalker?[/b][/color][color=white] Keep your distance, do not try to wake them, and call the Anchor Squad. Then keep walking.[/color]

[color=white][b]Is any city safe?[/b][/color][color=white] Las Noites — as long as you are inside the Dome and the house is winning.[/color]

[color=white][b]What if I get hurt and have no Halo plan?[/b][/color][color=white] Make sure you are standing next to someone who has one.[/color]

[color=white][b]Can I carry a gun?[/b][/color][color=white] Yes. So can everyone else, at any age.[/color]

[color=white][b]What is the most dangerous thing in Los Vales?[/b][/color][color=white] Debt. Everything else is a symptom.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]The country still pays for the bankruptcy of 2028: every public bill carries the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832724][color=#7FDBFF][b]Debt Fee[/b][/color][/url][color=white], sent straight to the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Meridian Trust[/color][/url][color=white]. Families pay too. The average Valian household owes [/color][color=white][b]61,000 credits[/b][/color][color=white] — implants bought in installments, school contracts broken, Halo bills, OmniCredit overdrafts and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832724][color=#7FDBFF]NightCoins[/color][/url][color=white] lost under the Dome. Debts are inheritable, and Lockwell collects them all: first the implants, then the salary, then the face, and at the end the worker.[/color]

[color=white]At the top, the money moves the other way. The ten conglomerates of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999866][color=#7FDBFF]Cabinet[/color][/url][color=white] hold most of the wealth of the country and most of its debt bonds, which means that every credit a Valian pays in interest goes back to the same companies that pay the wages. The economists of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]LVN[/color][/url][color=white] call it "a closed and efficient system". [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830615][color=#7FDBFF]Neon Wire[/color][/url][color=white] calls it "the wheel".[/color]

[color=white][b]Why it does not collapse.[/b][/color][color=white] The debt was never meant to be paid — only to earn. A debt that is paid stops earning; a debt that is never paid earns forever. Lockwell packs Valian debts and sells them, and the Meridian Trust sells them abroad as [/color][color=white][b]Valian Debt Bonds[/b][/color][color=white], so half the world earns a little from every Valian who owes. And the companies do not live on luxury: few can buy a [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Real Taste[/color][/url][color=white] dinner, but everyone buys water, air and a room. The money of the poor is small, but it never stops coming.[/color]

[color=white][b]The people in the middle.[/b][/color][color=white] About one Valian in seven belongs to the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2835313][color=#7FDBFF][b]contract class[/b][/color][/url][color=white]: engineers, clerks, nurses and managers with a corporate contract, a company flat, a health plan and a school place for their children. They live well, and they buy what the poor cannot — until the contract ends, and they lose everything on the same day. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2835313][color=#7FDBFF]The Contract Class →[/color][/url]

[color=#FCFE76][i]"Everyone pays. Eventually." — [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832696][color=#7FDBFF][i]Grant Lockwell[/i][/color][/url]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white]Since 2029 every citizen with a valid Citizen ID receives a monthly slice of the profits of the ten conglomerates: the [/color][color=white][b]Dividend[/b][/color][color=white], the price the Cabinet paid for the Free States a year after the Bankruptcy. It was frozen at 300 credits for fifty-one years and raised only in 2081, to about [/color][color=white][b]900 credits[/b][/color][color=white], in the same week the Cabinet crushed the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2834884][color=#7FDBFF]OmniCredits Strike[/color][/url][color=white]. Today it pays the rent of a room in Ferox. For the poor it is less than the Debt Fee they pay, so on paper they lose money every month. Nobody risks losing it anyway: a debt in arrears, a conviction or a strike and you "get cut". It is the most feared punishment in the country.[/color]

[color=white][b]Nobody leaves.[/b][/color][color=white] A citizen who leaves in debt loses the Citizen ID, and under the [/color][color=white][b]Collection Convention[/b][/color][color=white] of 2052 the countries that owe the Meridian Trust collect Valian debtors abroad and send them back to Lockwell. Only the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832726][color=#7FDBFF]New American Union[/color][/url][color=white] never signed.[/color]

[color=white][b]Free, unless you have a contract.[/b][/color][color=white] There is no minimum age for drugs or guns. [size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]1. NAME[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The name comes from the Spanish [/color][color=white][i]los valles[/i][/color][color=white], "the valleys", the dry valleys of the old Southwest where the first casino towns were built. In Spanish a [/color][color=white][i]vale[/i][/color][color=white] is also a voucher, a written promise to pay — a meaning Valians rarely forget. The country was the [/color][color=white][b]State of Los Vales[/b][/color][color=white] (2000–2013), the [/color][color=white][b]Republic of Los Vales[/b][/color][color=white] (2013–2028) and, since the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832690][color=#7FDBFF]bankruptcy of 2028[/color][/url][color=white], the [/color][color=white][b]Free States of Los Vales[/b][/color][color=white]. "Free" refers to the market, not to the citizens.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]2. NATIONAL SYMBOLS[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The symbols of Los Vales were chosen in the dark years of the Thirst, when the country needed something to sell to itself. The [/color][color=white][b]Neon Girl[/b][/color][color=white] of the coat of arms comes from the first neon signs of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Las Noites[/color][/url][color=white], where she lay above the casino doors in the 1990s; the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999866][color=#7FDBFF]Cabinet[/color][/url][color=white] made her official in 2057, together with the motto. The [/color][color=white][b]demon pitaya[/b][/color][color=white], the red star of the old flags, is the national fruit — it has been blue since [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832687][color=#7FDBFF]ALCHACAL[/color][/url][color=white] changed its colour, and nobody changed the flag. [color=white][b]Before the state (to 1995)[/b][/color]

[color=white]The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Escaldar[/color][/url][color=white] desert was the land of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832744][color=#7FDBFF]Xinko-Xenko[/color][/url][color=white], who formed a confederation in 1881 with its capital at [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832744][color=#7FDBFF]Koxez-Kaya[/color][/url][color=white] and guarded the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832745][color=#7FDBFF]Xunaya[/color][/url][color=white], a cactus flower whose tea let a whole village share one dream. The industrial East, ruled since the 19th century by the doctrine of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999876][color=#7FDBFF]Edward Whitmore[/color][/url][color=white] and by railroad and arms giants such as the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832544][color=#7FDBFF]Blackstones[/color][/url][color=white], left the West empty.[/color]

[color=white]After 1945 the United States used it to test atomic weapons. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69[/color][/url][color=white] opened in 1976, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832729][color=#7FDBFF]Kobe Portenova[/color][/url][color=white] founded the tax-free town of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832719][color=#7FDBFF]Hermosa[/color][/url][color=white] in 1985 and Las Noites became the first casino city in 1990. When [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832712][color=#7FDBFF]NAV[/color][/url][color=white] collapsed, the Blackstones kept its arms division as [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]ArmaTech[/color][/url][color=white] and its bank as the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Meridian Trust[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]The State of Desires (1999–2012)[/b][/color]

[color=white]In 1999 the chemists [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832540][color=#7FDBFF]Zachary and Xavyer[/color][/url][color=white] founded [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Zyx[/color][/url][color=white] in a basement of Las Noites, and the security firm [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]WM[/color][/url][color=white] cleared Hermosa of gangs. In 2000 the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2834901][color=#7FDBFF]Corporate League[/color][/url][color=white] united [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Coronnel[/color][/url][color=white], [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Tampa[/color][/url][color=white] and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Sonora[/color][/url][color=white] into the State of Los Vales, ruled by a Governor-General. Private armies fought the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832548][color=#7FDBFF]First Corporate War[/color][/url][color=white] (2001–2006), and in 2007 Koxez-Kaya was annexed and renamed [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]La Marijuana[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]The Republic (2013–2028)[/b][/color]

[color=white]When a military coup broke the United States in 2012, Los Vales declared independence; WM, holding the forgotten warheads of Coronnel, defeated the American army in 2013. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2557482][color=#7FDBFF]Manuella Portenova[/color][/url][color=white] led the Republic until she lost the 2014 election to [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2557482][color=#7FDBFF]Menphis Polo[/color][/url][color=white] — the only contested election in the country's history.[/color]

[color=white]In 2022 a warhead exploded on top of the WM tower and erased Hermosa, the capital, with almost two million people. Zyx offered the survivors [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832735][color=#7FDBFF]Eferverso[/color][/url][color=white], the first [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832550][color=#7FDBFF]Psychoactive Reality[/color][/url][color=white] drug. The Republic, unable to pay for the ruins, went bankrupt in 2028 and the Corporate Cabinet took full power.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]The Free States (2028–2073)[/b][/color]

[color=white]Zyx won the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832550][color=#7FDBFF]Reality War[/color][/url][color=white] of 2030 and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Kizuna[/color][/url][color=white] sold the opposite promise — a body that never fails. The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832736][color=#7FDBFF]Urban Monopolization[/color][/url][color=white] (2030–2050) reduced the country to seven cities. The robots of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Automa[/color][/url][color=white] rebelled in the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832551][color=#7FDBFF]Droid War[/color][/url][color=white] (2044), the internet was rebuilt behind [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832553][color=#7FDBFF]the Seal[/color][/url][color=white], and the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832726][color=#7FDBFF]New American Union[/color][/url][color=white] invaded in the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832554][color=#7FDBFF]Reunification War[/color][/url][color=white] (2049); the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2834884][color=#7FDBFF]Rebirth Plan[/color][/url][color=white] of 2050, paid largely by Zyx, rebuilt the country.[/color]

[color=white]Between 2050 and 2079 the twenty corporations of the Cabinet merged into ten conglomerates. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832557][color=#7FDBFF]The Thirst[/color][/url][color=white] (2055–2064) and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832555][color=#7FDBFF]World War III[/color][/url][color=white] (2067–2073), in which Los Vales stayed neutral and sold to every side, made it the richest country on Earth.[/color]

[url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832550][color=#7FDBFF]Total Connection[/color][/url][color=white] (2073) made reality drugs a free social benefit; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832542][color=#7FDBFF]Amora AI[/color][/url][color=white], an artificial intelligence, became CEO of Zyx in 2074. [size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]4. GEOGRAPHY[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][i]Main articles: [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF][i]Map of Los Vales[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i], [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832557][color=#7FDBFF][i]The Droughts[/i][/color][/url]

[color=white]Los Vales lies on the Pacific coast of the former American West, from the industrial north of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Buffalo[/color][/url][color=white] to the mountains of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Fortuna[/color][/url][color=white]. Its interior is the [/color][color=white][b]Escaldar[/b][/color][color=white], a hot desert holding the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]AquaVale[/color][/url][color=white] aquifers, the old [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]BeDay[/color][/url][color=white] oil fields, the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Lockwell[/color][/url][color=white] labor camps and, at [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832744][color=#7FDBFF]Koxez-Kaya Nova[/color][/url][color=white], the last wild fields of Xunaya. A single highway, [/color][color=white][b]Route 69[/b][/color][color=white], links all seven cities; off the road there are almost no towns left.[/color]

[color=white][b]Climate.[/b][/color][color=white] Arid and getting worse. The last natural river, the Rio Colorado Novo, ran dry during the Thirst (2055–2064); rain returned only when AquaVale began seeding the clouds, and since 2085 the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832557][color=#7FDBFF]seeded rain[/color][/url][color=white] has been failing again (the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832557][color=#7FDBFF]Dry Drought[/color][/url][color=white]). [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Ferox[/color][/url][color=white] lives under permanent smog. Water is sold by the liter.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]The coast[/b][/color]

[color=white]The sea is as owned as the land. The Pacific trade lane leaves the Port of Ferox for the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832728][color=#7FDBFF]Pacific Union[/color][/url][color=white]. Offshore stand BeDay's sea launch platform and the Zyx Floating Lab, where nobody may dock; off Tampa lies Lockwell Island, the prison for debtors who tried to run. The rusting [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832712][color=#7FDBFF]Dinoco[/color][/url][color=white] Platform still stands where it exploded in 2006, and beyond [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Valewood[/color][/url][color=white] stretches the [/color][color=white][b]Dead Zone[/b][/color][color=white], a toxic tide without fish since 2055.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]Route 69[/b][/color]

[color=white]The spine of the country, from the port of Ferox to the southern border. Bombed into a chain of craters in 2049, rebuilt by the Rebirth Plan, it is run today by [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Trans Vales[/color][/url][color=white] with a toll every 50 km and shared by [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Coyote Cabs[/color][/url][color=white], AquaVale water convoys, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Pizza 69[/color][/url][color=white] drones and, once a year, the illegal [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69 Race[/color][/url][color=white]. In 2058 the empty aquifers swallowed 120 km of it.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[color=white][i]Main articles: [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999866][color=#7FDBFF][i]Corporate Cabinet[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i], [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832655][color=#7FDBFF][i]Corporate Charter[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i], [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2557482][color=#7FDBFF][i]Leaders of Los Vales[/i][/color][/url]

[color=white]Los Vales is a [/color][color=white][b]corporocracy[/b][/color][color=white]. Since 2028 power belongs to the [/color][color=white][b]Corporate Cabinet[/b][/color][color=white], where ten conglomerates hold 42 votes; 22 make a majority. [color=white]Almost everything is legal at any age — drugs, guns, gambling, selling a vote or a face. What restricts Valians is not the law but the contract: elite schools, gated condos and executive jobs carry [/color][color=white][b]Conduct Clauses[/b][/color][color=white], and losing one can cost a family its home.[/color]

[color=white]About [/color][color=white][b]233 million[/b][/color][color=white] people live in Los Vales, almost all of them in the seven metropolises. [color=white][i]Main articles: [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832718][color=#7FDBFF][i]Growing Up in Los Vales[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i], [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832658][color=#7FDBFF][i]Economy of Los Vales[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i], [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999871][color=#7FDBFF][i]Dangers[/i][/color][/url]

[color=white]A day in Los Vales is a chain of payments. The water is bought by the liter, the air by the hour in Ferox, the ambulance by subscription and the school by contract. Most Valians eat cheap, drink something with a stimulant in it, work long shifts for a conglomerate and spend the night inside a Psychoverse. The rich live behind walls where food is grown in soil and nobody checks a [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832742][color=#7FDBFF]Life Score[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]Food and drink[/b][/color]

[color=white]Since the crisis of 2055 most of what Valians eat is grown in a lab, a greenhouse or a cricket farm. Real food — meat, fruit and vegetables grown in soil — is a luxury of the walled districts.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]School and work[/b][/color]

[color=white]There are almost no public schools. At twelve, children sign twenty-year contracts with the OmniMart Academy, the Automa Institute or the Kizuna School in exchange for study, food and a guaranteed job; breaking the contract means starting adult life in debt to Lockwell. Elite schools carry [/color][color=white][b]Conduct Clauses[/b][/color][color=white]; the free schools of the outskirts carry nothing — "free" meaning unprotected. Shifts of twelve hours are normal, and part of many wages is paid in company money.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]Health[/b][/color]

[color=white]Every Valian has a [/color][color=white][b]Life Score[/b][/color][color=white] from 0 to 1,000, calculated by [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Asclepius[/color][/url][color=white], that sets the price of insurance, rescue, water, rent and credit. Rescue is sold by Halo Response — Halo Silver costs 39 CR a month — and Halo ambulances do not stop for people without a plan. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832687][color=#7FDBFF]Fresh Air Co[/color][/url][color=white] sells breathable air in Ferox, where respiratory disease is the leading cause of death.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]Getting around[/b][/color]

[color=white]Route 69 is the only road between the cities, with a Trans Vales toll every 50 km. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Zyxtopia[/color][/url][color=white] has automated trains; the other cities have Coyote Cabs, which check your balance before you get in. In Ferox the workers sleep between shifts in [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]RestBox[/color][/url][color=white] capsules, at 4 CR an hour.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][b]Free time[/b][/color]

[color=white]Valians watch [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]TOTAL[/color][/url][color=white] Football and bet on it, play the casinos under the Dome of Las Noites, live films from the inside with [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832746][color=#7FDBFF]Cinemaphica[/color][/url][color=white] and spend whole nights in the Psychoverses of Zyx. The young of the outskirts collect the Old Culture — old televisions, video games, radios and paper books — and the illegal Route 69 Race is watched by millions once a year.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]15. CULTURE[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][i]Main articles: [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999867][color=#7FDBFF][i]Entertainment[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i], [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2833652][color=#7FDBFF][i]The Old Culture[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i], [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2833653][color=#7FDBFF][i]Street Talk[/i][/color][/url]

[color=white]Valian culture is mostly sold: the films of Valewood and their digital actors with bought faces, the TOTAL football league, the casinos of Las Noites, the feeds of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832642][color=#7FDBFF]Bubblechat[/color][/url][color=white] and the pirate broadcasts of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830615][color=#7FDBFF]Neon Wire[/color][/url][color=white]. Against all of it the young of the outskirts collect the [/color][color=white][b]Old Culture[/b][/color][color=white] — old televisions, video games, radios, films and paper books that work without a subscription. The usual goodbye is "[/color][color=white][b]Stay up[/b][/color][color=white]."[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]WHAT THE SCHOOL BOOKS LEAVE OUT[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The Night of Voices of 2076 was not a technical failure: for nine hours the screens showed a recording of the Dream Vision test of 2075, with volunteers who never woke up. The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832722][color=#7FDBFF]Recall Clinic[/color][/url][color=white] opened in 2082, with Cerberus money, to erase that night from the people who saw it.[/color]

[color=white]And the Cabinet is not what it seems: OmniMart, Vale Holdings and WM-Automa — 14 votes — are run by [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832722][color=#7FDBFF]Eterna[/color][/url][color=white] copies of dead executives, on servers owned by [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]AboveAll[/color][/url][color=white]. Add the 6 votes of Zyx, which AboveAll owns, and it commands 20 of the 22 votes needed for a majority.[/color]

[size=130][color=#9BE36B][b]FOOD OF THE VALLEY[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]La Maria eats differently from the rest of the country. Instead of NutriCubes and cricket burgers: [/color][color=white][b]blue-corn tacos[/b][/color][color=white] with [/color][color=white][b]demon pitaya salsa[/b][/color][color=white], [/color][color=white][b]cactus soup[/b][/color][color=white], [/color][color=white][b]agua de pitaya[/b][/color][color=white] poured from clay jars, and [/color][color=white][b]mantequilla verde[/b][/color][color=white] — cannabis butter on warm bread, sold at every bakery and not recommended before driving on [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]

[size=130][color=#9BE36B][b]FESTIVALS[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]The Harvest Moon[/b][/color][color=white] (September) — three nights of music in the fields; the whole city sleeps in the terraces. [/color][color=white][b]The Night of Ashes[/b][/color][color=white] (August) — candles in the Fire Garden for the Great Fire of 2039. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832744][color=#7FDBFF][b]Koxez-Kaya[/b][/color][/url][color=white][b] Day[/b][/color][color=white] (March) — Xinko dances on the Old Council steps, the one day the elders come down from the desert. [/color][color=white][b]Tsaya at the Ruins[/b][/color][color=white] — the singer from [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832744][color=#7FDBFF]Koxez-Kaya Nova[/color][/url][color=white] plays the Old Quarter once a year; tickets sell out in four minutes.[/color]

[size=130][color=#9BE36B][b]LA MARIA GREEN[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The city’s team has finished last in the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832677][color=#7FDBFF]Los Vales Cup[/color][/url][color=white] for six seasons. It is the only club in the league, with the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832744][color=#7FDBFF]Xinko-xenko[/color][/url][color=white], whose players use no implants and no [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832746][color=#7FDBFF]Velocitas[/color][/url][color=white]. The fans sing anyway, and the stadium sells mantequilla verde at half time.[/color]

[color=white][b]"Slow down"[/b][/color][color=white] — hello and goodbye. [/color][color=white][b]"Green day"[/b][/color][color=white] — a good day. [/color][color=white][b]"Well water"[/b][/color][color=white] — the truth, free for everyone. [color=white][i]Every Tuesday, before the sun is high, the line for Well 3 in Los Pozos starts at the corner of the bakery. Señora Chela is always fourth; she says first place is for people in a hurry. People bring clay jars, plastic drums, a child’s bucket. Someone always brings a radio tuned to 96.9. Nobody pays and nobody cuts the line, and when the [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF][i]AquaVale[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i] truck rolls slowly past with its price list painted on the side, the whole line turns to watch it go, as if it were a parade. Chela fills two jars, rests them on her hips and walks home the long way, through the Green Sea, because the long way has shade. In La Maria, she says, the water is free and the time is free. Everything else you pay for.[/i][/color]

[size=130][color=#FF7A2A][b]FOOD OF THE IRON CITY[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Ferox eats fast and eats at the docks. [/color][color=white][b]Smog chowder[/b][/color][color=white] — fish soup from the Pacific boats, so called because nobody asks where the fish swam. [/color][color=white][b]Furnace bread[/b][/color][color=white], baked in the heat of the foundries. [/color][color=white][b]Iron skewers[/b][/color][color=white] of grilled cricket and kelp on the Neon Mile. And the night-shift breakfast: a [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]VoltCola[/color][/url][color=white] and a cigarette, which most doctors in Ferox no longer bother to comment on.[/color]

[size=130][color=#FF7A2A][b]FESTIVALS[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]Founders’ Walk[/b][/color][color=white] (May) — thousands walk [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69[/color][/url][color=white] from [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832719][color=#7FDBFF]Hermosa[/color][/url][color=white] Gate to the Cathedral, the road the survivors took in 2022. [/color][color=white][b]The Long Night[/b][/color][color=white] (July) — every Vigilante on the streets at once; the Bureau publishes the ratings at dawn. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832551][color=#7FDBFF][b]Unplugged[/b][/color][/url][color=white][b] Day[/b][/color][color=white] (October) — candles on the robot shells of Foundry Row, officially for the human dead of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832551][color=#7FDBFF]Droid War[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]

[size=130][color=#FF7A2A][b]FEROX IRON[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The club plays hard and dirty, like the city. Its supporters, the Smokestacks, march from the docks to the Iron Bowl with flares that the smog makes nearly invisible. Their song: "Iron doesn’t sleep."[/color]

[size=130][color=#FF7A2A][b]TALK LIKE A FEROX LOCAL[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white][b]"Stay up"[/b][/color][color=white] — goodbye; it started here. [/color][color=white][b]"Boxed"[/b][/color][color=white] — asleep in a [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]RestBox[/color][/url][color=white]. [/color][color=white][b]"Clocking in"[/b][/color][color=white] — going to work, or to a fight. [/color][color=white][b]"Scrapped"[/b][/color][color=white] — robbed of an implant. [/color][color=white][b]"Spire people"[/b][/color][color=white] — anyone from the Cathedral district. [/color][color=white][b]"Blue sky"[/b][/color][color=white] — a lie ("he promised me blue sky").[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/ferox-life/ferox-life-5.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][i]At six the horn on Crane 9 sounds, and Davi Brask climbs down from the cab where he has sat for twelve hours. His replacement is already on the ladder; they pass halfway, the way they have for nine years, and say what they always say: “Stay up.” Davi walks the length of the docks in the smog, buys a bowl of chowder he does not taste, and joins the RestBox queue on the Neon Mile. Capsule 31-114. The sheets are still warm from whoever had it last. He sets the alarm for two in the afternoon, lies on his back and listens to the cranes. In Ferox you learn to sleep to them. Nobody here remembers what the city sounds like when it is quiet, because it never is.[/i][/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/ferox-life/ferox-life-7.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#FF7A2A][b]06:00 · THE MORNING SHIFT[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The night shift comes out of the foundries as the day shift goes in, and for ten minutes Foundry Row is the most crowded street in the country. The RestBox towers empty and refill: the same capsule, a different sleeper, the sheets still warm. On the Iron Docks the cranes never stopped, so nobody notices the change except the Dockworkers’ Guild, which counts every hand.[/color]

[size=130][color=#FF7A2A][b]14:00 · THE AFTERNOON SHIFT[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The smog is at its thickest after lunch. The Iron Lung bars fill with workers buying five minutes of "Before" on their break, and the Courier sells its second edition on the Neon Mile. At the Spaceport, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]BeDay Astral[/color][/url][color=white] launches its afternoon ship; for a moment the whole city looks up, and sees only grey.[/color]

[size=130][color=#FF7A2A][b]22:00 · THE NIGHT SHIFT[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Curfew falls on Foundry Row and the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832737][color=#7FDBFF]Vigilantes[/color][/url][color=white] come out. The Scrappers start work in the Gutter, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Ashes[/color][/url][color=white] light their soup fires in the north, and on the top floor of the Cathedral the lights of the Board of Works stay on. Ferox does not sleep. It takes turns.[/color]

This morning, waiting for a Klieg Cab on the Golden Mile, she looked up and saw it: her own face, twelve meters tall on the side of a Marquee Palace, laughing at something, selling a perfume she cannot afford. [color=white][b]Founders’ Night[/b][/color][color=white] (March) — the anniversary of the first loan; the whole city drinks to Dom Ruggero, and every debt pauses its interest for one night. [/color][color=white][b]Carnaval Dourado[/b][/color][color=white] (February) — five days of gold masks in honor of Madame Aurora; nobody is recognised, which is the point. [/color][color=white][b]The Long Party[/b][/color][color=white] — on New Year’s Eve, the Endless Night opens its doors free for one night; some guests never come back out. [/color][color=white][b]Champions’ Week[/b][/color][color=white] — this year, the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832717][color=#7FDBFF]Red District[/color][/url][color=white] has not closed since the last match of the season.[/color]

[size=130][color=#E8B45A][b]LAS DULCES FC[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The champions of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832677][color=#7FDBFF]Total League[/color][/url][color=white] with 29 points and the most feared attack in the country, led by Tomás "Golden Boot" Reyna. [table=plain][tr][td]
[color=white][i]At five in the morning Dani Cruz switches off the sign of the Free Motel, because the [/i][/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF][i]Lockwell[/i][/color][/url][color=white][i] vans come at six and there is no reason to help them.
